look_here_first: Start with several adult leaves: chinkapin oak has an elongated chestnut-like blade with many regularly spaced teeth, each served by a near-parallel lateral vein; its sharp/forward-pointing teeth have NO red-oak terminal bristle. Turn over the leaf for a pale, minute stellate-hairy surface, and confirm a moderately sized acorn in a NON-fringed cup. Compare bur oak's midleaf waist and shaggy cup.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaf blade obovate to elliptic, usually unlobed to shallowly undulate

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: roughly 8–14 pairs of strong parallel secondary veins ending in regular marginal teeth

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: lower leaf surface pale/glaucous with minute stellate hairs

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: bark light to medium gray, thin and flaky/scaly

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: acorn matures in one season; cup commonly encloses about one-quarter to one-half of nut

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Leaves usually 50–150 × 40–80 mm, leathery, obovate or sometimes narrower, margins regularly undulate/serrate, teeth often strongly antrorse (forward-pointing) but lack red-oak bristles.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Secondary lateral veins usually 10–14 near-parallel pairs reaching evenly spaced marginal teeth; look at multiple mature leaves.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Abaxial surface pale/glaucous and seemingly nearly glabrous, but minute appressed symmetric 6–10-rayed stellate hairs occur; adaxial mature blades often glossy.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Acorns commonly 1–2, sessile or on stalk up to 8 mm; cup 4–12 mm deep × 8–22 mm broad, encloses 1/4–1/2 nut; cup scales tuberculate but NOT long-fringed.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Acorn nut generally 15–20 mm long (range 13–28 mm), 1-year maturation; bur oak nuts often substantially larger.

key_traits.label: Oak training
key_traits.text: Use leaf architecture plus bark/twig/buds and mature acorn/cupule; never identify an oak from leaf silhouette alone.
